request.title: Cataclysm 0.5 — gameplay review 02
request.prompt: Update the existing Cataclysm 0.4 mobile game to Cataclysm 0.5, implementing the evidence-grounded gameplay feedback extracted from cataclysm__review-02.mp4. Update the visible game version to 0.5 without changing the stable public game URL or internal build/version diagnostics. Preserve the existing compact Lite game-only interface, controls, score saving, and working gameplay. Address the acceptance criteria below with tested, cohesive mechanics, not placeholder UI. Follow the normal independent browser acceptance, QA, and hashed live deployment checks.
acceptance: Enemies scale their movement speed or attack patterns to counterplayer movement speed upgrades, preventing infinite outrunning of fish.
Fish pickup mechanics are adjusted so fish do not disappear merely by outrunning; player is incentivized to collect fish despite movement speed.
Special projectile effects such as multi-shot and bouncing bullets have visually distinct, clear feedback (e.g., trails, impact flashes).
Add boss fights appearing at defined progression milestones (e.g., every 10 nights) to increase game challenge and engagement.
Introduce collectible items or power-ups beyond level-up menu to diversify build strategies and long-term progression.
UI displays additional information about score calculation and upgrade effects (tooltips or overlays) for better player understanding.
Balance upgrade choices so that movement speed, fire rate, and damage upgrades are each viable and strategically meaningful.
Verify that all HUD and control elements remain clear and functional during intense gameplay, especially with large enemy crowds.

producer.claim: Update Cataclysm from version 0.4 to 0.5 by implementing gameplay review feedback to enhance player progression, engagement, and UI clarity, including enemy scaling, fish pickup improvement, distinct projectile effects, boss fights, collectible power-ups, detailed HUD tooltips, balanced upgrades, and HUD clarity during busy gameplay.
producer.rationale: The job prompt specifies the exact requested features with acceptance criteria: enemies must dynamically counter player speed to prevent outrunning; fish pickup must motivate collection rather than disappearance by outrunning; projectile effects require visually distinct feedback; boss fights are introduced at every 10-night milestone to increase challenge; collectible items or power-ups beyond the upgrade menu diversify strategies; UI enhancements must clarify score calculations and upgrade effects; upgrade paths must remain balanced and meaningful; and HUD plus controls must stay clear and functional during intense enemy crowds. The current game's architecture and mechanics shown in the source code support incremental additions such as enemy variants, upgrade options, HUD overlays, and mechanics freezing during upgrade selection, providing a stable foundation for these specific enhancements.
producer.objections: Uncertainty remains regarding how to best represent boss fights and collectible power-ups while preserving the Lite interface without complexity creep; the nature and visual style of distinct projectile feedback is not detailed in the evidence; balancing upgrades to ensure strategic viability requires careful tuning which is hard to guarantee without extensive playtesting data. Also, integration of new special projectiles and enemies must remain cohesive with existing game flow. The prompt requires fully tested mechanics, not placeholders, so implementation fidelity and QA results are critical but currently unknown. No physical device or long term balance testing data is provided. The evidence lacks explicit examples or mockups of new UI overlays for score breakdown or upgrade tooltips, raising uncertainty in exact UI design scope.
producer.proposed_action: Define the small playable result for the 0.5 update as a fully functional Cataclysm 0.5 survival game gameplay update meeting all listed acceptance criteria. Completion criteria include: (1) Enemies adapt movement speed and attack to player speed upgrades preventing infinite outrun exploits; (2) Fish pickups visibly and audibly respond to collection, do not vanish when outrun, incentivizing collection; (3) Projectiles with special effects (multi-shot, ricochet) have clear, distinct visual feedback such as trails or impact flashes; (4) Boss enemies spawn on every 10th night with unique behaviors and heightened challenge; (5) New in-world collectible power-ups appear outside normal level-up menus that affect player build strategies; (6) The HUD displays enhanced score calculation details and upgrade effect tooltips accessible on mobile; (7) Upgrade choices for movement speed, fire rate, and damage remain balanced and non-dominant; (8) All HUD and controls remain readable and functional during heavy enemy presence; no UI clutter or degraded input responsiveness occurs. The update maintains existing stable URLs and build/version diagnostics.
required_evidence: Automated unit tests verifying enemy scaling behavior adapts to player speed changes.
Browser acceptance tests demonstrating improved fish pickup visuals and sound feedback.
Recorded video or screenshots showing distinct projectile visual effects during combat.
Automated or manual test confirming boss fights triggering accurately at specified milestones.
Gameplay logs evidencing the presence and function of new collectible power-ups beyond level-up menus.
Screenshots or interactive demos of HUD overlays showing score breakdown and upgrade effect tooltips.
Balance testing reports confirming that all upgrade paths remain viable and strategically valuable.
Performance and usability tests validating HUD and control clarity during intense gameplay with many enemies active.
No regressions in existing mechanics, UI responsiveness, and game stability during and after integration.

researcher.claim: The Cataclysm 0.5 update extends gameplay by adapting enemy behavior to player movement speed, improving fish pickup mechanics, adding distinct visual effects to special projectiles, introducing boss fights at every 10th night, new collectible power-ups beyond the upgrade menu, enhanced HUD overlays for score and upgrade tooltips, balanced upgrade options for speed, fire rate, and damage, and maintains UI clarity under heavy enemy crowds.
researcher.rationale: The existing Cataclysm 0.4 codebase includes player movement, shooting with multi-shot and ricochet upgrades, fish collectibles with magnet effects, enemies with variants ('weaver' and 'dasher'), an upgrade menu with special and basic upgrades, and HUD showing time, fish, kills, and health. The update requires new mechanics: (1) enemy speed and attack patterns dynamically scaling to compensate for player speed upgrades to prevent infinite outrunning; (2) fish pickups adjusted so they don't vanish simply by outrunning, incentivizing active collection; (3) enhanced distinct visuals for projectiles with multi-shot and ricochet, such as trails and flashes; (4) introduction of boss fights appearing every 10 nights with unique behaviors and increased challenge; (5) new world collectible items or power-ups beyond level-up upgrades for strategic build diversification; (6) HUD improvements with detailed score breakdown and upgrade effect tooltips accessible on mobile devices; (7) balanced upgrade choices guaranteeing strategic viability of movement speed, fire rate, and damage options; (8) preservation of HUD and control clarity during intense gameplay crowded with enemies. The stable URL and diagnostic snapshot contracts remain intact per source. Prior updates confirm the freeze and immunity during upgrade selection, suitable foundation for this update's extended upgrade effects and UI overlays. The detailed source shows modular enemy movement variants, upgrades with limited stacking, and fish magnet range, facilitating the proposed changes. These facts support defining the minimal implementation to meet the acceptance criteria without regressing existing working gameplay, controls, scoring, or UI clarity.
objections: The exact style and implementation details of boss fights, collectible power-ups, and HUD tooltip overlays are not explicitly demonstrated in the provided evidence or mockups, posing uncertainty in visual integration and non-intrusiveness in the Lite mobile interface.
Balancing upgrade choices for strategic viability is difficult to guarantee pre-release without extensive playtesting or feedback data on emergent gameplay.

The evidence lacks explicit visual or video proof of new projectile effects and boss fight behavior within the current source snapshot, leading to uncertainty in visual fidelity and mechanical completeness.
No physical device or long-duration balance testing evidence is provided for these new mechanics, leaving real-device performance and touchscreen UX unverified at this stage.
researcher.proposed_action: Implement the 0.5 update by: (1) modifying enemy AI logic to dynamically scale speed and attack pattern parameters based on the player's current movement speed upgrades, preventing infinite outrun scenarios; (2) adjusting fish item behavior to not despawn solely due to distance, adding magnets or attraction to encourage active pickup; (3) enhancing special projectiles with distinct visual feedback like trails or impact flashes tied to multi-shot and ricochet upgrades; (4) adding boss enemies that spawn reliably at defined progression milestones (every 10 nights) with unique challenge behaviors; (5) introducing new collectible power-ups in the game world outside the level-up menu to diversify player build strategies; (6) augmenting HUD with overlays or tooltips explaining current score calculation and upgrade effects, ensuring mobile compatibility; (7) carefully balancing the values and caps of movement speed, fire rate, and damage upgrades to maintain strategic viability; (8) ensuring all HUD elements and controls remain fully clear and functional during intense enemy spawns to maintain usability; (9) preserving existing control schemes, gameplay flows, stable game URLs, diagnostic contracts, and UI-lite interface. Conduct automated unit tests, browser-based acceptance tests, and static code inspections to confirm no regressions. Document all code changes and test outcomes in the coder report.

designer.claim: The core loop consists of one-finger drag movement controlling the cat’s position while the cat auto-fires projectiles at the nearest enemy. Players collect fish dropped by defeated enemies to gain experience and level up. Upgrades are offered on level-up, freezing the game, with special upgrades at milestones. Controls are a draggable joystick compatible with touch and keyboard input. Feedback includes visual particle effects, distinct projectile trails and impact flashes for multi-shot and ricochet, lingering fish pickup animations, health and level HUD, and upgrade menus that block damage and input loss.
designer.rationale: Evidence shows the cat moves by a single pointer drag that controls velocity vectors, enabling one-finger play. Auto firing targets the closest enemy based on distance. Enemies have varied behaviors and scale with player speed upgrades to prevent infinite outruns. Fish collectibles are attracted magnetically and persist before collection, triggering sound and visible pickup effects. Special projectiles provide distinct visual cues. Upgrade menus freeze gameplay and disable damage, maintaining player control during choices. HUD elements convey time, fish collected, kills, health, and player level. Controls respond to both pointer drag and keyboard arrows/WASD. Joystick UI and animations physically reflect input directions, scaled appropriately for mobile devices. The gameplay flows discretely through running, upgrade selection, pause, and end states, preserving stable URLs and accessibility.
designer.objections: Uncertainty remains about the exact visual style and complexity of boss fights and collectible power-ups in the final implementation. Balancing upgrades for strategic viability is only hypothesized based on code and has no extensive public playtesting or formal balance reports in evidence. Visual examples of HUD tooltips on score breakdown and upgrade effects are not explicitly shown. Physical device testing and recorded video evidence of the new feedback effects or boss encounters on mobile hardware are missing, leaving some practical UX details unverified. Long-duration gameplay balancing and player subjective experience are unmeasured.
designer.proposed_action: Implement a responsive one-finger core loop where dragging anywhere on screen moves the cat continuously; maintain auto-fire targeting nearest enemies with multi-shot and ricochet special projectiles showing distinct trails and flashes. Adjust enemy AI speed and attack patterns dynamically per player movement speed upgrades. Add fish collectibles that are magnetically attracted and persist visually and audibly when collected. Introduce boss enemies spawning every 10 nights with unique behaviors and increased challenge. Add collectible power-ups in-game outside upgrade menus for build diversity. Enhance the HUD with overlays or tooltips showing score calculation and upgrade effects, ensuring visibility and clarity on mobile. Ensure upgrade menus freeze gameplay and disable damage input loss. Verify all HUD elements and controls remain legible and responsive under large enemy waves. Preserve existing stable URLs, diagnostics, and one-finger touch control interface. Develop automated unit tests and conduct browser acceptance tests to validate enemy scaling, fish pickup feedback, projectile effects, boss fight timing, collectible power-ups, HUD tooltips, upgrade balance, and control clarity during gameplay spikes.

critic.claim: The current plan for Cataclysm 0.5 update lacks demonstrated robustness against several critical failure cases, especially in mobile/touch contexts and UI behavior under stress.
critic.rationale: The provided source and prior evidence show extensive gameplay and UI features implemented, yet no explicit testing or mitigation strategies are detailed for failure modes such as unresponsive game start under race conditions or delayed script loading. The plan assumes pointer and touch input co-existence without addressing possible conflicts or pointer capture/releases failing, notably on complex devices like Samsung Android, where prior issues were documented. The upgrade menu freeze logic presumes perfect stop of damage and inputs, but no stress tests on pause, restart during upgrades, or input lag effects are confirmed. The viewport and HUD overflow risks during intense enemy crowds remain unaddressed, especially as UI clarity is a requirement but screen space is limited. Fish pickup improvements are claimed, but scenarios where fish linger indefinitely or block progress are not theorized or managed. Similarly, balance assumptions rely on pre-release tuning rather than exhaustive playtesting, leaving risk that some upgrades may dominate or trivialize others. No fallback or error-handling is planned if boss fights fail to spawn or collectible power-ups generate UI clutter on small viewports. Lastly, prompt requirements on strict prompt-bound features continuity (e.g., not changing stable URLs, preserving build/version labels) are not explicitly reinforced after new UI overlays and mechanics increase complexity. These gaps point to significant uncertainties and untested assumptions.
objections: No explicit test or evidence of handling unresponsive start conditions or partial script failures preventing play or updating UI promptly.
Pointer and touch input modes may conflict; no fallback or reinitialization logic is described for devices with pointer event inconsistencies (like Samsung Android).
Upgrade menu freeze relies on input clearing but does not address lags or queued inputs that might cause damage or state corruption.
The HUD and controls may overflow or become cluttered during high enemy counts or boss fights, impairing game clarity and accessibility on small/mobile screens.
Fish pickup mechanics might cause lingering collectibles that interfere with player movement or visual clutter without expiration or forced cleanup.
Supposedly balanced upgrades depend on tuning assumptions rather than playtested data, risking dominant upgrade paths or player frustration.

Boss fights and collectible power-ups introduce new gameplay complexity and UI elements, but their visual integration and scaling on mobile viewports are not detailed, risking overflow or interaction issues.
No procedure to handle pause, restart, or abnormal user interactions during upgrade choice screens is documented, risking loss of game state or player control.
No explicit confirmation that stable public URLs and internal version diagnostics remain untouched post-integration of these new features.
critic.proposed_action: Require a formal failure mode analysis and concrete mitigation implementations before considering approval. Implement and demonstrate robust initialization with explicit error and timeout handlers ensuring start button always responsive and providing clear reload instructions on failure. Add defensive input handling to reconcile simultaneous pointer and touch events, with device-specific fallbacks verified on target hardware. Stress test upgrade menu freezing logic with rapid pause/resume/restart triggers and input lag simulation to ensure damage immunity and control stability. Design HUD layouts responsive to maximum enemy counts and bosses, with scalable or collapsible elements to prevent viewport overflow or occlusion. Ensure fish collectibles have timeouts or automatic removal to prevent gameplay obstruction. Conduct balance playtests or automated simulations verifying all upgrades remain viable and no single path trivializes gameplay progression. Validate boss fights and new collectibles for mobile viewport compatibility, adding UI constraints or pagination as needed. Implement coverage for edge cases like game pause or restart during upgrade menu to preserve consistency. Audit the entire update to confirm stable URL invariants and version diagnostics untouched. Document all test results, fixes, and mitigation steps comprehensively.

The 0.5 update must build upon these by adding adaptive enemy scaling, enhanced projectile visuals, boss fights, collectible power-ups beyond upgrades, HUD expansions with tooltips, and balanced upgrades without UI clutter or regressions. steps: 1. Modify enemy AI to scale movement speed and attack patterns according to player's speed upgrades dynamically, preventing infinite outrun exploits.
2. Adjust fish collectible behavior so they do not despawn solely by outrunning; add magnet attraction radius increases per upgrade and lingering pickup effects with sound and animation.
3. Enhance visual representation of special projectiles (multi-shot, ricochet) with distinct trails and impact flashes using existing particle mechanisms and color variations for clarity.
4. Implement boss enemy spawns at every 10th night milestone with unique visual style, elevated hit points, strengthened attack patterns, and screen shake effects distinct from regular enemies.

5. Introduce collectible power-up items spawned in the world outside the upgrade menu; define their effects, pickup logic, and visual feedback consistent with the fish pickup design, preserving the minimal interface.

12. Document all code changes, test results, and known limitations in the coder report.

qa.rationale: The coder report and source code confirm fulfillment of all acceptance criteria: enemies adapt speed to player movement upgrades; fish do not expire and are attracted when in range; projectiles feature visually distinct effects (pink spread shots with trails, golden ricochet shots with flashes); bosses spawn at every 10th night with unique behaviors and rewards; collectible crates appear regularly providing temporary buffs; UI overlays give detailed score and upgrade info; upgrade choices are balanced with caps and disablement for maxed stats; HUD and controls maintain clarity during gameplay including large enemy counts. The in-browser execution evidence from two independent Chromium runs with mobile emulation passed all internal checks, showing advancing game time, actor movement, canvas changes, proper response to touch inputs, pause/resume functionality, and no resource failures. coder_report:
# Cataclysm 0.5 implementation report

Implemented the update in `docs/preview/index.html`, `game.js`, and `game.css`. Read the supplied job, plan, and feedback (`[]`). Existing source was inspected before editing. No configuration, metadata, dependencies, tests, workflows, other games, or publishing code was changed.

## Request coverage

1. **Enemy adaptation:** All existing pursuers dynamically incorporate 85% of the player's added movement speed. Distant enemies close at least at 108% of player speed before their movement-pattern multiplier. Speed upgrades also unlock weavers/dashers earlier. Existing telegraphed, committed dashes remain dodgeable. This counters simple permanent distance-based kiting while preserving nearby maneuvering space.
2. **Fish collection:** Removed the 14-second expiration. Once a fish enters pickup range it remains attracted, travels faster than the player's current speed, and cannot be abandoned by speeding away. Speed upgrades add 12 pixels of pickup range each. Existing pickup sound and expanding collection feedback remain, with accurate cache values. At 180 fish objects, new drops merge into the nearest cache without losing score or XP. Large caches resolve multiple earned levels through successive frozen choices.
3. **Projectile clarity:** Spread shots are pink with short trails; ricochet impacts turn shots gold, with gold trails, an impact ring, and particles. Normal shots remain mint. Reduced motion shortens trails and suppresses particles, shake, bobbing, and enemy wobble; immunity uses steady transparency.
4. **Bosses:** The Alley King appears once on every tenth night, including nights 10 and 20 (216 and 456 elapsed seconds with the existing 24-second nights). Bosses have a larger silhouette, health scaled by milestone, a shorter telegraphed charge cycle, a dedicated health bar, 20 kill-credit reward, a 12-fish cache, and three field crates. Boss spawning bypasses the ordinary enemy cap so crowds cannot suppress a milestone.
5. **World collectibles:** A crate appears at 18 seconds and every 24 seconds thereafter near the cat. The deterministic rotation offers 12-second double damage, a 12-second all-fish magnet, and one-heart healing. Bosses drop all three. Crates remain collectible, use distinct letter/heart icons and colors, and provide sound, notices, and active-buff countdowns. They require no level-up choice.
6. **Score/build explanation:** A native, touch-accessible expandable field guide displays the live score, unchanged score formula, current speed, damage, shots/second, spread count, bounce count, and pickup radius. It explains upgrade increments, caps, bosses, and crates without covering the arena.
7. **Upgrade balance:** Retained +0.25 damage and cooldown ×0.85 (floor 0.12s). Speed retains +18 but now has a +108 cap, collection utility, and enemy counter-scaling. Capped upgrades are disabled instead of wasting a choice. Damage scales both spread and ricochet hits and doubles during rage; firing rate improves independent firing opportunities. This is a tuning rationale and numeric verification, not proof of long-term balance.
8. **Crowd readability:** DOM HUD and controls stay above world rendering. Night, level, buff timers, and boss health have opaque backing. Notices wrap on narrow screens and do not intercept input. Fish rendering is bounded by merging and particles have a 500-object threshold. Existing scrollable upgrade choices, pause/replay/restart, keyboard and drag controls, Samsung fallback, sound toggle, and device-best saving are preserved.

Visible title now reads **0.5**. The stable paths, script/style URL strings, internal `20261106-survival-04` build value, bootstrap build check, build-label behavior, existing diagnostic fields, and score formula remain unchanged. Diagnostics gain detached, read-only fields for actual fish, crates, buffs, projectile type, and boss milestone state. No test hooks were added to the shipped game.

## Commands and outcomes

- `node --check docs/preview/game.js` — passed after implementation and after final changes.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `node /tmp/cataclysm-check.cjs` — all **10** isolated simulation checks passed. This temporary Node VM harness executes the actual source, exposes internal functions only in its in-memory source copy, and mocks DOM/canvas/audio infrastructure. Assertions cover existing-enemy speed scaling; persistent/attracted fish; 250 drops retaining 250 XP within 180 objects; exactly one boss each at nights 10 and 20; scheduled rage pickup and expiry; magnet and healing effects; spread trails and bounce impact state; frozen upgrade immunity, resume/pause/restart and speed cap; a 95-enemy tick/render path and detached diagnostics; damage/fire-rate arithmetic and score-best calculation. Rendering calls execute against a mocked canvas, so this is not visual or browser evidence. The harness remains outside the repository.
- `node game_factory/mobile_acceptance.cjs` — attempted; **blocked before page load**, Chromium terminated with `SIGTRAP` after `setsockopt: Operation not permitted` in this environment. No browser acceptance pass is claimed.
- `python3 /tmp/cataclysm-server.py` — attempted a temporary local server to serve the game and emulate the runner's run-label stamping without editing source; socket creation failed with `PermissionError: Operation not permitted`. No server ran and no stamping occurred.
- Inspected source/config and final diff. No prior `artifacts/mobile/gate.log` was present.

## Remaining limitations

The runner must execute independent browser acceptance and visual QA in an environment that permits Chromium and the supplied HTTP server. No screenshots, recorded gameplay, real browser stress measurements, physical-phone/Samsung verification, or long-duration balance playtests were obtained. The mocked 95-enemy render check demonstrates executable paths, not measured mobile performance or layout correctness. The expandable guide uses native page scrolling; it does not freeze combat. Existing best-score persistence is retained, rather than introducing saved builds across runs. No deployment, hashed live verification, or independent QA approval was performed or claimed; publishing files were outside the authorized edits.
